assumptions: computational verification data includes solved quadratic-residue primes
denominator patterns generalize beyond the verified range

proposals.structural_violation_claim: Every identity/covering family in the sources keys its constructions to fixed small moduli, and the reciprocity obstruction confines such methods to quadratic non-residues. This move instead mines the certified solutions that large-scale verification already produced for the historically awkward quadratic-residue primes within the finite range, seeking a parameterization of their denominators (for example, how the successful first denominator x relates to the divisor structure of n) that is not expressible as a fixed-modulus congruence condition. The claim that such a non-congruence pattern exists and extrapolates is a hypothesis, not an established result.
proposals.novelty_argument: The verification source is treated in the bundle only as evidence and instance supply; none of the listed mechanism families uses the solved quadratic-residue instances as training data for a candidate parameterization. The change is mechanistic, not verbal: the operator is pattern extraction over certified solutions rather than identity assembly over residue classes, and its output is required to break the fixed-modulus keying that the obstruction analysis shows is the conserved failure structure.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: Split the solved quadratic-residue instances into a fitting set and a held-out set. Fit any candidate denominator rule on the first set and test whether it predicts a valid decomposition on the held-out set. If no rule beats per-instance search, or every extracted rule reduces to a fixed-modulus congruence condition, the direction fails cheaply without any new theory.

assumptions: solutions of one n induce solutions of related n
orbit closures can reach survivor classes
breaks: fixed-modulus covering as the coverage notion

proposals.structural_violation_claim: The covering-system attempt fails because coverage is defined as a finite union of fixed congruence classes, which reciprocity confines to non-residues. This proposal replaces congruence-class coverage with orbit coverage: use the induced-solution maps from the structural solution-set analysis to propagate known solutions from solved n to quadratic-residue primes, asking whether the orbit of the solved set under these maps reaches every survivor. Whether the maps' reach escapes the residue/non-residue dichotomy is an open hypothesis; the obstruction as stated governs congruence relations, and it is not established that it governs orbit reachability.
proposals.novelty_argument: The sources use induced-solution maps only to organize and link classes, not as the primary coverage mechanism. Switching the coverage object from residue classes to dynamical orbits changes the operator set and the locality of the argument rather than relabeling an existing family; the reciprocity obstruction was proved against congruence relations and does not obviously transfer.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: Enumerate the explicit induced-solution maps available from the structural analysis, apply them exhaustively to a seed set of small solved n, and check computationally which quadratic-residue primes below a modest bound are reached. If the reachable set is itself describable by fixed-modulus congruence conditions, or misses survivor primes that direct search solves, the orbit-coverage idea fails at low cost.

assumptions: known parameterizations are slices of one variety
new slices may exist beyond the congruence-derived ones

proposals.structural_violation_claim: The variety lift is reported as organizing known mechanisms without adding positivity: its known slices correspond to congruence-derived parameterizations, all confined to non-residue classes. The proposed move is to search the variety for rational slices or sections that were not obtained from any congruence identity, on the hypothesis that a slice whose specialization covers quadratic-residue classes must exist there if any polynomial-style construction crosses the wall at all. That such a slice exists is unverified; the proposal only relocates the search to a space where non-congruence constructions would be visible.
proposals.novelty_argument: The sources use the lift for unification and transport of counting arguments; none uses the variety as a generative search space for new slices. The mechanism changes from re-representation of known families to enumeration of new rational subobjects, and it carries a built-in discrimination test: any slice found must be checked for whether it secretly reduces to a fixed-modulus congruence, in which case reciprocity already dooms it.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: Before any open-ended search, derive from the reciprocity obstruction a necessary condition that a wall-crossing slice must violate, and check whether the variety's structure as described forces every rational slice to satisfy the congruence-reducibility property. If every slice provably specializes to fixed-modulus congruence data, the direction is closed cheaply; otherwise a bounded search for low-degree slices, tested against known solved quadratic-residue instances, gives an early empirical verdict.

representations: solution-count function restricted to survivor classes
assumptions: sieve estimates remain applicable on the restricted ensemble
restricted averages are informative about the hardest cases
preserves: mean solution density on the restricted family
breaks: averaging over all primes as the ensemble

proposals.structural_violation_claim: The averaging approach bounds the mean solution count over all primes, and its stated boundary is that polylog average growth cannot force per-prime existence, with rare primes possibly having none. The proposed move restricts the ensemble to exactly the quadratic-residue survivor classes and asks for both a mean and a variance (or concentration) statement there. The hypothesis is that if the restricted mean stays comparable to the unrestricted one while the variance is controlled, the fraction of survivor primes with zero solutions can be bounded much more tightly than the sources report; this is an unproven analytic claim, and it would still not by itself prove existence for every prime.
proposals.novelty_argument: The sources average over all primes and observe degradation for square-like primes as a side effect; none makes the survivor family the ensemble or targets a second-moment statement on it. Changing the ensemble and adding a variance objective changes the analytic mechanism, not the vocabulary, and it directly probes whether the zero-solution scenario is measure-theoretically crowded out on the wall itself.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: Compute empirical solution-count distributions for quadratic-residue primes within the already-verified computational range and compare mean and spread against all primes. If counts on the survivor family are systematically depressed toward zero or heavy at low values, the concentration hypothesis fails before any sieve work is invested.

assumptions: the first denominator may depend on the full divisor structure of n rather than its residue class
auxiliary_objects: representation-count estimates for the reduced rational

proposals.structural_violation_claim: The two-fraction reduction degrades for square-like primes because, with x chosen by class-level recipes, the divisor structure of 4/n minus 1/x does not guarantee a split. The proposed move makes the choice of x a function of n's individual divisor data rather than its residue class: characterize, for square-like n, which x values make the reduced rational's numerator-denominator pair divisor-rich, and prove a criterion under which at least one admissible x always exists. That such an adaptive criterion covers all quadratic-residue primes is a hypothesis; the reciprocity obstruction constrains congruence-keyed selection but is not shown in the sources to constrain divisor-adaptive selection.
proposals.novelty_argument: All constructive families in the bundle select constructions from residue-class membership; the factorization scheme exposes per-n divisor structure but is reported as giving no global organization. Fusing the two — per-n divisor data steering the two-fraction reduction — changes the selection operator itself, which is the component the obstruction analysis identifies as congruence-bound, rather than renaming the reduction.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: For quadratic-residue primes in the verified range, tabulate which first denominators x actually admit two-fraction splits (recoverable from certified solutions plus bounded recomputation) and test whether any divisor-structural predicate on (n, x) separates working from failing x. If no predicate beats residue-class baselines, the adaptive-selection premise fails cheaply.

representations: Type A and Type B solution forms
assumptions: the proposed congruence system is checkable per prime
a counterexample would lack both forms

proposals.structural_violation_claim: The Type A/B congruence system self-declares its completeness as conjectural: either some prime lacks both forms or the reformulation is at least as hard as the original. Rather than proposing a new construction, this direction stress-tests that open completeness claim exactly where every prior family fails — on quadratic-residue survivor primes — searching for a prime admitting solutions but of neither Type A nor Type B form. Any outcome is reported as a scoped empirical finding, not a proof about all primes.
proposals.novelty_argument: The bundle records the Type A/B proposal but no adversarial test of it; the sources' verification effort predates or is independent of the form classification. The mechanism is a challenge operation targeted at the newest structure's weakest joint, and its information yield is asymmetric: a neither-form prime immediately falsifies the covering hope, while persistent coverage on the hardest classes concentrates future effort on proving the system rather than widening it.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: Take quadratic-residue primes within the already-verified range, classify each certified solution by whether it matches the Type A or Type B form, and look for a prime whose entire solution set (within search bounds) avoids both. A single such prime ends the completeness conjecture; the check reuses existing certificates and bounded search only.

assumptions: the reciprocity obstruction as stated governs fixed-modulus congruence relations
broader method families may or may not inherit it
preserves: confinement of congruence methods to non-residues

proposals.structural_violation_claim: The obstruction analysis proves congruence-carried identities cannot eliminate quadratic residues, but the sources leave the exact scope of the wall informal: it is not stated whether divisor-adaptive constructions, induced-solution orbits, or non-congruence variety slices are also covered. The proposed move formalizes the method families and attempts to extend or delimit the obstruction: prove for each family either that it reduces to congruence relations (and so is blocked) or exhibit the precise structural feature that escapes the reduction. The claim that a sharp boundary exists and is provable is a hypothesis; the deliverable is a map of which proposal families above are already dead.
proposals.novelty_argument: The bundle contains one obstruction result and many constructions, but no analysis of the obstruction's own boundary. Working on the meta-level object — the predicate 'reduces to fixed-modulus congruence data' — is a different operator from both constructing solutions and proving the original obstruction, and it directly prices every other direction: extensions kill proposals cheaply, and any proved non-extension certifies a genuinely open lane.
proposals.cheapest_falsification_path: Attempt the reduction argument first for the easiest candidate family (finite sets of polynomial parameterizations in n). If even that family resists both reduction to congruence data and any counterexample construction after a bounded effort, the boundary-mapping program is likely intractable at current tools and should be dropped; if it reduces immediately, the extension has positive value and the next family is attempted.
